title: Amel programme workers’ sit-in seeking resolution of employment status
location: Nouakchott, in front of the General Delegation for National Solidarity and the Fight against Exclusion (TAAZOUR) buildings
threshold_50_evidence: Not established: the search-result text calls the participants a group of workers but supplies no attendance estimate. Workforce counts in other results are not protest attendance.

title.summary: Search-result text identifies a sit-in by graduates employed in the Amel programme.

start_date.summary: Search-result text is dated 20 January 2021 and says the sit-in occurred “today”; the source remains unopened/search_only.

location.summary: Search-result text places the sit-in before TAAZOUR buildings in Nouakchott.

organizer.summary: The article says a group of programme workers acted; no named organizer is given in the snippet.

demands.summary: Snippet says participants sought resolution of their legal status, activation of TAAZOUR’s higher committee, and presidential intervention including regularization and placement in state institutions.

participants_original.summary: No participant estimate in the search result.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or qualifying qualitative crowd description in the search result; threshold remains unverified.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown; no opened source provides this information.

state_response.summary: All seven response fields remain unknown; the available search-result snippet gives no event-specific response.

end_date.summary: Unknown; no source identifies a physical end or last day of activity.

notes: Search-only discovery lead. Do not infer assembly size from the number of workers represented by the claim. A separate Le360 article published 4 January describes recurrent Amel-worker sit-ins but does not date its “latest sit-in”; whether it is this episode, a prior event, or an out-of-month event is unresolved.
open_questions: Can the 20 January report be opened or independently corroborated?
Was at least 50 people assembled at this specific sit-in?
What were the physical end and state responses?
Is the recurring presidential-palace sit-in mentioned by Le360 before or during January, and is it separate from the 20 January sit-in?

title: Koylal plain sit-in against land allocation and irrigation works
location: Koylal plain, Mbagne department, Brakna region (Mauritania)
organizer: Residents / land users from Feralla; the report attributes the action to mobilized local populations but does not name a formal organizing body.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The retrospective report says a mobilization call by the populations and a sit-in occurred, but gives no attendance number or qualifying crowd description.

title.summary: The FPC report identifies a sit-in in the Koylal plain associated with recovery of land claimed by local communities.

start_date.summary: A spokesperson quoted at a 23 March press conference said mobilization began on 22 January and a sit-in was organized the same day.

location.summary: Report places the sit-in in the Koylal plain in the Mbagne department; it identifies the landholders as Hebbiyabé/Yirlaabé communities and names Feralla.

organizer.summary: The report attributes mobilization to local populations and land users; formal organizer not established.

demands.summary: Spokesperson says the mobilization sought return of ancestral lands amid state-allotted PARIIS irrigation works.

participants_original.summary: No attendance number stated for the 22 January sit-in.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The source supplies no count or qualitative crowd-size description for January 22.

state_response.summary: No event-specific January 22 state response established. Later February events and official visits are not attributed to this gathering.

end_date.summary: No physical end or last activity date for this sit-in is established.

notes: Retrospective occurrence claim only. S008 says farmers threatened a sit-in, and S016’s timeline dates that threat to 25 January; those accounts may refer to the same action or a different stage but do not resolve whether/how the January 22 gathering occurred. S014 separately reports a February 22 gathering. Do not infer January attendance or response from the later event.
open_questions: Can contemporaneous January reporting verify that the sit-in occurred on 22 January?
Was at least 50 people physically assembled?
What was the duration and any event-specific state response?
How does the Jan22 sit-in relate to Jan25 threat reports and the Feb22 sit-in?

title: Gold prospectors protest Maaden Mauritania mining-area closure
location: Chami area; exact mining site unclear (the report also names “منطقة تفرغ زينة”)
participants_original: المئات من المنقبين إضافة إلى ممثلي النقابات إلى المنطقة رافضين القرار جملة وتفصيلا
threshold_50_evidence: The search-result text describes protests and says hundreds of prospectors plus union representatives came to the area rejecting the closure. This is a qualitative crowd-size claim that would exceed 50 if it refers to simultaneous protest participants; the article does not fully clarify that relationship and remains search_only for this researcher.

title.summary: Al-Hurriya search result reports protests by gold prospectors against mining-area closures by Maaden Mauritania.

start_date.summary: The visible 1 January 2021 date is publication date; the article text does not state the protest occurrence date. Start date remains unknown; unit-month inclusion is provisional.

location.summary: The title and text place the prospectors and protests in the Chami area; the exact mining site is unclear, with the report also naming “منطقة تفرغ زينة”.

organizer.summary: The source mentions prospectors and union representatives but does not identify a formal organizer.

demands.summary: The article says protestors opposed a closure decision by Maaden Mauritania and called on authorities to intervene; official S019 establishes Maaden as a public institution under ministerial technical supervision.

participants_original.summary: The Arabic phrase says hundreds of prospectors plus union representatives came to the area rejecting the decision; exact simultaneous protest attendance is not explicit.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Hundreds of prospectors” is a qualitative crowd description likely above 50 if it refers to the protest gathering; the relationship is ambiguous and the article is search-only for this agent.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown; no event-specific report establishes protester violence.

state_response.summary: All seven state-response fields unknown. The appeal to authorities is a demand, not a response.

end_date.summary: Unknown; no source establishes physical end date or later activity.

notes: Provisional discovery candidate in the January unit. The article is visibly dated 1 January 2021, but that is publication date, not a stated occurrence date; onset and month ownership are unresolved and may fall in an adjacent month. Do not assign 1 January as start date. The reported “hundreds” may describe a protest crowd but is not an exact count. S019 confirms Maaden Mauritania’s public-institution status from 2020. Keep separate from the 22 February Chami protest over a new tax/ore-transport fee (S017–S018).
open_questions: When did the protest actually occur, and is January the month of onset?
Does “hundreds came to the area” refer to concurrent protest participants?
What exact mining site is meant by Chami and “منطقة تفرغ زينة”?
Were there any event-specific state responses or end date?

title: Service-provider teachers’ meeting seeking integration into the civil service
location: Nouakchott (article reports through a Nouakchott correspondent; exact meeting venue not stated)
organizer: Service-provider teachers’ union; coordinator Sidna Abdallah is named, but formal union name is not visible in the result.
participants_original: 300 teachers attended a press conference transformed into a meeting (report wording: “300 enseignants ont assisté à la conférence de presse transformée en meeting”).
threshold_50_evidence: The RFI-republished report explicitly says 300 teachers attended the Jan17 meeting, a source-reported count above the 50-person threshold. The report is search_only for this researcher and the exact venue/public access are not visible, so eligibility remains pending review.

title.summary: RFI report describes a teachers’ press conference transformed into a meeting.

start_date.summary: The report is dated Monday 18 January and says the meeting occurred “this Sunday,” implying 17 January 2021.

location.summary: The report is filed by its Nouakchott correspondent, but the meeting venue is not specified.

organizer.summary: The report identifies the participants as service-provider teachers and names their union coordinator Sidna Abdallah; formal union name is not visible.

demands.summary: The teachers seek integration into the civil service after passing a national competition; S023 and opened S027 describe regularization/public-service status as the central demand. This is a labor-status demand directed to the Ministry/public service.

participants_original.summary: Report states 300 teachers attended the meeting; the distinct figure of 3,600 refers to competition-admitted teachers, not attendees.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The report states 300 people attended the meeting, exceeding 50 if the meeting is accepted as a public assembly; source access and venue remain uncertain.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown; no source establishes protester violence at this gathering.

state_response.summary: No source establishes any of the seven responses to this specific meeting. The Jan22 Ministry statement S024 is about the broader dispute, with no explicit link to this gathering.

end_date.summary: Unknown; no source establishes the physical end of the meeting.

notes: The report’s 18 January publication date and “this Sunday” wording imply a 17 January meeting; start_date is based on that relative-date conversion and remains source-result-only. It says 300 teachers attended a press conference transformed into a meeting, which may be a qualifying public assembly but venue/open access require review. The separately planned sit-in outside the Education Ministry on Monday is not confirmed as executed and is not merged with this meeting. The issue concerns service-provider teachers, not the Amel-programme workers at TAAZOUR in E001. Do not use the workforce figures (3,600 in the RFI report and more than 4,000 in the Jan1 letter) as participants. Opened S027 confirms the public-service demand but is a letter, not a Jan1 gathering.
open_questions: Can the RFI report be independently opened or corroborated?
What was the exact meeting venue, and was it open as a public assembly?
Did the separately planned Monday Ministry sit-in occur, and what was its turnout?
What event-specific response or physical end is documented?
How did the Jan17 meeting relate to the wider service-provider campaign that began in December and the Jan23 strike suspension?
